About Anthropic
Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.
As Partner Account Manager you will help manage and execute the partnerships that accelerate Claude adoption, unlock new capabilities and drive outcomes for our joint customers across Germany, Austria and Switzerland.
You will own a defined set of named partners end to end — a mix of (a) in-country DACH practices of our global system integrators (e.g. Accenture, Deloitte, Capgemini, PwC, BCG), where you work hand in hand with the GSI alliance owners who hold the global relationships, and (b) regional system integrators, consultancies and AI-native boutiques that DACH enterprises and the Mittelstand actually buy from. The DACH partner book is split between you and the Head of Partnerships DACH and CEE; for every partner assigned to you, you own the plan, the enablement path, the co-sell motion with our DACH sales team and the partner-sourced and partner-influenced pipeline that results from it. This is a builder role: partner-sourced pipeline in DACH is still a small fraction of our open pipeline, and there is a first playbook but no established machine. We need someone who has taken partnerships from zero to a repeatable revenue engine in this market before, not someone who has inherited and administered an existing partner book.
Key responsibilities
Partner development and execution:
Run each partner as a structured pursuit: stakeholder map (country lead, AI/data practice lead, alliance lead, key account partners), joint account plan, agreed target accounts and a quarterly cadence.
For your assigned GSI country practices: activate the DACH teams against the global frameworks and translate them into concrete joint accounts. For your assigned regional SIs / boutiques: build the relationship from scratch (selection, onboarding into the Claude Partner Network, enablement, first joint deals).
Guide partners in building repeatable Claude offerings (agentic engineering rollouts, agentic use cases, enterprise adoption programs) for the priority DACH industries: automotive and manufacturing, financial services and insurance, public sector, telco, pharma and chemicals.
Drive co-selling with the DACH AEs, Applied AI and Technical Success teams: introduce partners into the right accounts, bring partner-sourced opportunities to sales, and make sure every partner-attached deal is tagged correctly in Salesforce.
Performance and KPI ownership:
Own and drive the KPIs for your portfolio: Partner delivered use-cases, partner-sourced pipeline, partner-influenced pipeline and revenue, consultants enabled and certified, partners progressing through CPN tiers, joint proposals submitted.
Establish clear success metrics with each partner and drive regular business reviews against targets
Report on partnership health, progress, and commercial outcomes with data-driven insights
Every deal that runs through your partners must be set up for customer success and expansion: agree success criteria for joint accounts, make sure the partner delivers implementation and adoption support, and feed what you learn back into our partner program and the DACH sales team.
Market development and brand building
Represent Anthropic in the DACH partner ecosystem — partner events, joint customer events, and partner-led marketing in German.
Adapt the global partner playbook to DACH buying behaviour (Mittelstand vs. DAX/SMI enterprises, long procurement cycles, works councils, preference for local delivery partners) and decide deliberately what not to copy.
Navigate the regulatory and sovereignty topics that come up in almost every DACH deal (GDPR, EU AI Act, data residency, regulated industries such as banking and insurance) together with the partner and our internal experts.
Build differentiated joint value propositions with partners so that Claude is the default recommendation of the DACH consulting ecosystem.
You may be a good fit if you have:
Builder mentality — comfortable starting from a small base and turning it into a scaled partner business; you enjoy doing the work yourself.
8+ years of partner / alliances / channel experience with system integrators and consultancies in DACH, ideally at a cloud, data or AI platform company.
Existing relationships in the DACH practices of the large SIs and/or with the regional consultancies and boutiques — you know who runs the AI and data practices in Germany, Austria and Switzerland.
Data-driven, KPI-oriented and comfortable being measured on partner-sourced pipeline; a track record of driving incremental revenue through partners in DACH.
History of protecting the customer experience and the brand through partners — you say no to partners that cannot deliver.
Competitive drive — obsessed with winning and creating differentiation
Collaborative — you work as an extension of the DACH sales team and with Applied AI, Technical Success, partner marketing and the global GSI alliance owners.
Business-fluent German (C1+ / native) and English; able to run partner executive conversations and enablement sessions in German.
Based in Germany and willing to travel regularly within DE / AT / CH and occasionally to London and San Francisco.
Passion for AI and alignment with Anthropic's mission of beneficial AI development
Working Relationships
You will formally report to the International Partnerships leader, while your day-to-day work will be led by our DACH and CEE Partnerships leader who is based in Munich. You will also partner closely with Anthropic's regional sales leader and their Account Executives, as well as the in-region Customer Success and Technical Account Management teams.
Location and Travel
Based in Germany, ideally Munich; Berlin or Frankfurt are possible with regular time in Munich and with the sales team. Regular travel to partners and customers across Germany, Austria and Switzerland, plus occasional travel to London (partner leadership) and San Francisco (onboarding).

We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team.
Your safety matters to us.
To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. anthropic.com/careers
directly for confirmed position openings.
How we're different
We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills.
The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences.
Come work with us!

jobs.description: We made history and now we work to transform the future – for our customers, our communities and our families. You'll see your work on the road every day, helping people move freely and pursue their dreams. At Ford, you can build more than vehicles. Come build what matters. As part of our Manufacturing team, you’ll help build the world-class, state-of-the-art smart vehicles we're known for. In our plants around the world, we’re constantly developing new technologies and processes to further increase our efficiency. You'll get the satisfaction of making great products people use and love. We are seeking an experienced Manufacturing Engineer, Final Assembly to lead the development, design, and installation of production tooling in support of new F-150 program launches. In this role, you will drive tooling strategy from concept through implementation, ensuring all upper body tooling meets stringent quality, safety, and manufacturing efficiency standards. You will collaborate closely with cross-functional teams - including manufacturing engineering, quality, and program management - to ensure seamless integration of new tooling into production while meeting aggressive program timelines. Analysis of Release engineering designs for manufacturing feasibility Conduct manufacturing feasibility studies for the U81x ('31 Model Year) program Interface with plant teams to identify and use existing space for new program tooling and equipment Leading Cycle line layout meetings, setting up sequence of assembly and part orientation Lead in running simulations for tooling and design prove-out Understanding out-going quality on product line and applying lessons learned to the new vehicle line Write, update, and maintain program-specific process sheets for assembly of components DPA5 checks; raise part/process issues as identified to program; re-perform checks as D&R's CAD matures through UNV2 Support establishing virtual build sequence and support virtual build P-Release Complete design phase Health Chart assessments PFMEA creation and updates to support Conformance Letter Support Special Characteristics Cascade and Agreement Form (SCCAF) development and sign-off Develop program cost analysis (Vignette through PA) Define tooling needs, including: DC and pneumatic tooling Fixtured tooling and lift assists Ergonomic tooling needs Major equipment and/or automation needs Pallets, details, and subassembly build-up conveyance Error proofing Support cycle line layout development and workstation engineering work stream Support simulation development (provide benchmark data for equipment availability, MTTR, and MTBF) Ensure master schedule adherence Work with the Facility team to identify needs Develop tooling design and build SOWs, process RFQs, and supplier PO kick-off (re-assign POs to PI team at FDJ) Lead pre-FDJ shop buy-offs Bachelor's Degree in Engineering 1+ years' experience in a Manufacturing Engineering environment Knowledge of lean operating system; familiar with Kaizen principles Familiar with manufacturing environment RSLogix 5, 500, 5000; RSView and Factory Talk knowledge preferred Global Manufacturing Standard (GMS) and Vehicle Operation Structure Standard (VOSS) Industry standards – NFPA70E, NFPA79, ANSI, SAE HS-1738, UL 508A Implementation of error-proofing Problem-solving skills using statistics (Six Sigma Black Belt preferred) Ability to lead 8D MS Office application competency (Excel, Word, PowerPoint) Project management skills Strong interpersonal, written, and oral communication skills Ability to work with all levels of personnel for the duration of the program Ability to travel at times Preferred Qualifications: Some assembly tooling experience Production assembly experience preferred Lean manufacturing knowledge a plus Supplier project management skills preferred CPARS/MEARS/Ariba experience preferred Vision systems preferred FIS/IIOT reports (running and analyzing) preferred Competency in MTTR/MTBF preferred Automotive manufacturing experience preferred Knowledge of IT systems (AVS, EP, FIS, Networks) preferred Systems Engineering (Electrical and Mechanical) skills preferred You may not check every box, or your experience may look a little different from what we've outlined, but if you think you can bring value to Ford Motor Company, we encourage you to apply! As an established global company, we offer the benefit of choice. You can choose what your Ford future will look like: will your story span the globe, or keep you close to home? Will your career be a deep dive into what you love, or a series of new teams and new skills? Will you be a leader, a changemaker, a technical expert, a culture builder…or all of the above?
